description: Identify and copy-trade skilled Polymarket traders

00_initial.name: Initial Skilled Traders
00_initial.description: Identify and copy-trade skilled Polymarket traders
00_initial.hypothesis: Some traders consistently outperform and their patterns are detectable

analysis.summary: Core counts validated (238,953 traders, $8.6B volume match exactly), but the initial exploration has critical flaws: (1) it lacks actual PnL computation — proper token-aware PnL shows only 47% of $100K+ traders are profitable with negative average PnL (-$88K), invalidating volume-based 'skill' identification; (2) the top volume traders (highlighted as top-20) are actually the biggest losers (market makers losing $35-46M each); (3) the 'cheap_buys'/'expensive_sells' features conflate BUY/SELL side with YES/NO token direction.
key_insights: Volume is anti-correlated with profitability: the top-2 traders by volume ($124M and $97M) have the worst PnL (-$35M and -$46M respectively) — they are market makers, not skilled predictors
With proper YES/NO token-aware PnL, only 47% of $100K+ volume traders are profitable (median PnL: -$1,485), vs the naive 70% estimate that ignored token direction
52,516 traders (22% of 239K) have avg trade size under $5, likely bots or automated market makers that contaminate any skill signal
Only 21 of the top-100 volume traders maintain their rank across all three bi-monthly periods (Aug-Sep, Oct-Nov, Dec-Jan), showing very low rank stability
402,460 taker-only traders (with 39.7M trades) are completely excluded from the maker-only analysis, missing a large population of potentially skilled directional traders
BUY trades outnumber SELL 4:1 (136M vs 35M), creating strong bias in the cheap_buys feature which doesn't distinguish YES from NO tokens
concerns: CRITICAL: The 'unique_markets' metric of 63,143 is actually the MAX per-trader value, not the global count (actual: 245,029) — misleading summary statistic
CRITICAL: No PnL or profitability metric exists in the initial stage — volume tiers and activity tiers cannot distinguish skilled traders from market makers or noise traders

The cheap_buys/expensive_sells features are computed without token direction (YES/NO), so a BUY of a NO token at 0.45 is counted as a 'cheap buy' even though the trader is effectively shorting the event at 0.55
Resolution inference via last-trade-price is imperfect: ~10K markets (4.3%) have ambiguous last prices (0.05-0.95), and closed_at/resolved_at fields are all NULL in the markets table
Quantile values differ slightly between reported and ClickHouse validation (p50: 791 vs 786, p95: 35042 vs 38439), likely Float32 precision artifacts but worth noting
The lookback period (Aug 2025 - Jan 2026) is only 6 months; survivorship bias affects traders who started early in the period vs those who joined later

proposed_refinements.name: pnl_based_skill_scoring
proposed_refinements.description: Replace volume-based skill identification with proper PnL computation using token_market_map for YES/NO direction and inferred resolution from last trade prices on closed markets
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: Token-aware PnL will identify a distinct set of 'skilled' traders who differ from high-volume traders, with top PnL traders showing consistent positive returns across time periods
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Identify 200-500 traders with statistically significant positive PnL (>2 std above random), with at least 50% maintaining positive PnL across 2+ sub-periods

model_config_extra.token_direction: join token_market_map on asset_id for YES/NO outcome

proposed_refinements.name: bot_and_mm_filter
proposed_refinements.description: Classify and filter out market makers and bots before skill analysis using trade pattern signatures (tiny avg size, extreme trade frequency, symmetric BUY/SELL ratios)
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: Removing traders with avg_trade_size < $5 or trade_count > 500K (who account for 22% of addresses but are predominantly automated) will improve signal-to-noise in skill detection
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Reduce trader universe by 50-60K addresses while retaining 95%+ of total PnL variance; remaining traders show clearer skill separation

proposed_refinements.name: temporal_consistency_test
proposed_refinements.description: Split the 6-month period into 3 non-overlapping windows and measure PnL rank correlation (Spearman) across periods to test if skill persists
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: If trader skill is real and persistent, the Spearman rank correlation of PnL across consecutive 2-month periods should be >0.3 (vs ~0 for random); only 21/100 top-volume traders are stable, but PnL-ranked traders may show higher stability
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Spearman rho > 0.3 between adjacent periods for PnL-ranked traders, identifying a stable core of 50-200 consistently profitable traders

proposed_refinements.name: taker_side_analysis
proposed_refinements.description: Include taker-side trades in skill analysis since 402K taker-only traders with 39.7M trades are completely excluded from the current maker-only view
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: Taker-side traders who aggressively cross the spread may include informed traders with superior information, showing higher PnL per trade despite paying the spread
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Discover a meaningful subset of taker-heavy traders with positive PnL, potentially with different skill signatures (event timing, market selection) than maker-side traders

proposed_refinements.name: market_category_specialization
proposed_refinements.description: Test whether skilled traders specialize in specific market categories (sports, politics, crypto, etc.) and whether category-specific skill is more persistent than overall skill
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: Traders who concentrate in 1-2 market categories will show higher and more persistent PnL than diversified traders, because domain expertise is category-specific
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Identify category-specialist traders with >60% of volume in one category and significantly higher PnL/dollar than diversified peers

01a_pnl_based_skill_scoring.name: pnl_based_skill_scoring
01a_pnl_based_skill_scoring.description: Replace volume-based skill identification with proper PnL computation using token_market_map for YES/NO direction and inferred resolution from last trade prices on closed markets
01a_pnl_based_skill_scoring.hypothesis: Token-aware PnL will identify a distinct set of 'skilled' traders who differ from high-volume traders, with top PnL traders showing consistent positive returns across time periods

analysis.summary: The PnL-based skill scoring methodology is fundamentally sound — token-aware PnL correctly handles YES/NO positions, resolution inference via last-price shows zero contradictory markets, and the 180K market coverage is validated. However, a critical data gap exists: the analysis only uses maker-side trades, missing 17-44% (median 28%) of skilled traders' activity as takers, which could materially alter PnL rankings and the skilled/unskilled classification boundary.
key_insights: Token-aware PnL with 0.95 resolution threshold produces clean binary resolution (0 contradictory markets out of 180K), validating the resolution inference approach
Top PnL trader (0x6a72f...) confirmed: $80M maker volume across 1,666 markets, 88,080 buys vs 66 sells — almost pure buy-and-hold-to-resolution strategy
Only 88 traders (0.69% of 12,794) exceed 2σ threshold ($362K), with 63.6% showing multi-period consistency — genuine skill signal exists but is rare
PnL skill is distinct from volume: Spearman ρ=0.215 and only 40% overlap with top-volume traders, confirming the hypothesis that skilled traders differ from whales
The 12.7% of tokens with ambiguous last prices (0.05-0.95) are correctly excluded, preserving 180K clean markets for analysis
Sub-period market counts are highly uneven (36K→60K→106K), meaning the Dec-Jan period dominates consistency measurement
concerns: Extremely right-skewed PnL distribution (mean $10,975 vs median $184, ratio 60:1) makes the 2σ threshold very sensitive to a few extreme outliers inflating the standard deviation — consider robust alternatives like MAD or percentile-based thresholds
88 skilled traders is below the target range of 200-500 (skilled_in_target=false), suggesting the 2σ threshold is too aggressive or the population filters are too strict
Consistency metric is lenient: traders active in only 1 period get 100% consistency rate by default (e.g., 0xdc876e has periods_active=1, consistency_rate=1.0) — require minimum 2 periods active
Cross-sectional Sharpe ratio (mean_market_pnl / std_market_pnl) is not comparable to time-series Sharpe; median 0.084 is hard to interpret without benchmarking against random strategies
Survivorship bias: 60% of traders who started in Aug 2025 stopped before Jan 2026 — the qualifying population already selects for survivors
Effect size of 7.25σ is suspiciously large and likely inflated by the heavy-tailed distribution — bootstrapped confidence intervals would be more appropriate
No fee adjustment in PnL: makers pay 0% fees but their taker-side trades (omitted) would include fees — the true net PnL is slightly lower

proposed_refinements.name: include_taker_side_pnl
proposed_refinements.description: Incorporate taker-side trades into PnL calculation by unioning maker and taker views of trades_raw, giving complete position tracking per trader per token
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: Including taker-side trades will change PnL rankings for 60%+ of skilled traders and shift the skilled/unskilled boundary, since taker activity represents 28% of volume on average
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: More accurate PnL estimates; some currently-skilled traders may drop out while new ones emerge; population may increase toward the 200-500 target range

proposed_refinements.name: robust_skill_threshold
proposed_refinements.description: Replace mean+2σ threshold with robust alternatives (MAD-based, percentile-based, or winsorized statistics) to handle the extreme right-skew in PnL distribution
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: Using median + 3*MAD or a percentile-based threshold (e.g., top 2-4%) will produce a more stable skilled set in the 200-500 target range, less sensitive to extreme outliers
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Skilled count moves into the 200-500 target range; threshold is more stable across bootstrap resamples; identified traders have more homogeneous skill levels

proposed_refinements.name: strict_consistency_filter
proposed_refinements.description: Require minimum 2 active periods (out of 3) for consistency measurement, and equalize sub-period market exposure to prevent the 3x larger Dec-Jan period from dominating
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: Requiring ≥2 active periods will reduce false-positive consistent traders by 15-25%, and period-equalizing (e.g., sampling equal market counts) will produce more meaningful consistency rates
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Consistent-skilled count drops from 56 but remaining traders show more genuine persistence; consistency rate becomes a stronger predictor of future performance

proposed_refinements.name: risk_adjusted_ranking
proposed_refinements.description: Rank traders by risk-adjusted metrics (PnL per dollar, time-series Sharpe, or Calmar ratio) instead of raw PnL to identify capital-efficient skilled traders rather than just large-volume profitable ones
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: Ranking by pnl_per_dollar or a proper time-series Sharpe ratio will surface a different set of skilled traders who are more capital-efficient, with less than 30% overlap with raw-PnL top 88
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Identify smaller, high-efficiency traders who may be better copy-trade candidates; these traders likely have more concentrated, higher-conviction positions

proposed_refinements.name: bootstrap_significance_test
proposed_refinements.description: Bootstrap the skilled trader identification process to estimate confidence intervals on the threshold, effect size, and consistency rate — testing whether the 7.25σ effect size is robust
proposed_refinements.hypothesis: The 7.25σ effect size is inflated by heavy tails; bootstrapped 95% CI will show the true effect size is 2-4σ, and 10-20% of currently-identified skilled traders will not appear in >50% of bootstrap samples
proposed_refinements.expected_outcome: Calibrated confidence intervals for all key metrics; identification of which skilled traders are robustly identified vs. borderline; more honest effect size estimate

data_quality_issues.description: PnL calculation only uses maker-side trades, ignoring taker-side activity. For the top 10 skilled traders, taker-side volume represents 17-44% (median 28%) of total activity. Since every trade has both a maker and taker, a trader's position changes whether they are maker or taker. Missing taker trades means incomplete position tracking, potentially wrong net positions at resolution, and biased PnL estimates.
data_quality_issues.suggested_fix: Union maker-side and taker-side trades (with inverted side for taker: a taker BUY means they bought, same as maker BUY) before computing per-token positions. Query: SELECT maker as trader, side, ... UNION ALL SELECT taker as trader, side, ...

data_quality_issues.description: Population count shows minor discrepancy: stage reports 12,794 traders but independent ClickHouse validation with identical filters yields 12,796 (with resolution filter). Additionally, the top trader shows 1,666 resolved markets in ClickHouse but 1,625 in the stage output, suggesting subtle differences in join/dedup logic or timing.
data_quality_issues.suggested_fix: Verify that the stage's ClickHouse query uses FINAL keyword consistently and that the resolution-token join doesn't inadvertently drop condition_ids that have trades on only one token side

data_quality_issues.description: All neg_risk markets show neg_risk=false in the resolved population (0 out of 190,166). Only 70 neg_risk=true markets exist in the entire markets table. This means neg_risk market handling is untested but currently not impactful.
